reference: Internal Debts: A sum of ₹ 2,429.00 crore is estimated to be received from Internal Debts of the State.Internal Debts include various loans such as Market Loans which is projected at ₹ 900.00 crore, NABARD Loan is kept at ₹ 170.00 crore, National Co-operative Development Corporation Loan capped at ₹ 5.00 crore, Rural Electricity Corporation at ₹ 2.00 crore, Power Financing Corporation loan estimated at ₹ 2.00 crore and SIDBI loan of ₹ 350.00 crore.The Government vows to continue rural infrastructure development works through NABARD loans.Some of the major projects approved for funding under NABARD RIDF XXVII are Construction of CHCs, PHCs etc. & for Infrastructure and Logistic Supplies for Fighting the Ongoing Covid Pandemic with a total project outlay of ₹ 27.25 crore, Upgradation of Existing 17.9 km Road to Cement Concrete Pavement from Meidum - Hortoki (Phase-II) with a project amount of ₹ 133.66 crore, Construction of Separate 11kV Feeders for Power Supply to Agricultural Lands amounting to ₹ 12.25 crore, Soil Conservation Measures for Enhancement of Productivity in Mizoram with a total project cost of ₹ 10.00 crore and Six Irrigation Projects in Mizoram with a project amount of ₹ 10.47 crore. The State is also committed to take up more rural development projects in the coming Financial Year.
hypothesis: Internal Debts: The amount expected to be raised from internal debt is Rs. 2,429.00 crore. Internal debt includes loans proposed to be raised from various domestic institutions, namely market loans of Rs. 900.00 crore, NABARD loans of Rs. 170.00 crore, loans of Rs. 5.00 crore from the National Co-operative Development Corporation (NCDC), loans of Rs. 2.00 crore from the Rural Electrification Corporation (REC), loans of Rs. 2.00 crore from the Power Finance Corporation, and SIDBI loans of Rs. 350.00 crore. 882/2022-2023  
Mamit, 13th June, 2022: Shri Parshottam Rupala, Hon’ble Union Cabinet Minister, Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Govt. of India, today held a meeting at the DC Conference Hall, Mamit, with Government officials in Mamit town and beneficiaries under various Central Schemes. The meeting was chaired by Pu Lalnunhlua, District Bawrhsap, and Pu Lalsanglura, Nodal Officer of the Aspirational District Programme, gave a detailed PowerPoint presentation on the various activities under the Aspirational District Programme. The progress made and the various plans/initiatives were then discussed. Shri Parshottam Rupala, Union Minister, said that the purpose of his visit to Mamit District and the meeting was to see whether the various Central Schemes were benefiting the people of the district and being implemented properly, and that he had come to understand the difficulties and help resolve any problems that might arise. The District Concern Officers also explained the various Government programmes in detail and urged the beneficiaries to work hard so that they could definitely benefit from them. As Mamit District is an Aspirational District, the Central Government has made arrangements for up to Rs. 5 lakh to be billed for the treatment of serious illnesses, and he said that out of 5,000 people in Mamit District, 3,000 have already been selected to receive the benefit, while efforts are also underway to ensure that the remaining 2,000 can receive it. Speaking about PM-Kisan, he said that those who have Aadhaar Card, land records and bank accounts can apply, and he also urged the concerned departments to work so that farmers in Mamit District can receive as much benefit as possible from the scheme. According to the released draft electoral roll, 36-Tuichawng (ST) A/C has 15,852 male voters and 15,520 female voters, totaling 31,372; 37-Lawngtlai West (ST) A/C has 13,524 male voters and 13,402 female voters, totaling 26,926; 38-Lawngtlai East (ST) A/C has 11,626 male voters and 12,374 female voters, totaling 24,000; and in the three Assembly constituencies there are 41,002 male voters and 41,296 female voters, totaling 82,298. For the summary revision, those who wish to make representations will have time until January 15 of the new year. The final electoral roll is scheduled to be published on February 7, 2020. Along with this, 8 new polling stations have been added to the 62 polling stations in Tuichawng constituency, bringing the total to 70; 1 new polling station has been added to the 68 polling stations in Lawngtlai West, bringing the total to 69; and 7 new polling stations have been added to the 35 polling stations in Lawngtlai East, bringing the total to 42. Altogether, there will be 181 polling stations in the three constituencies of Lawngtlai District.

hypothesis: At Mamit, Children’s Week was observed today with a Fun Day programme organized by the District Child Protection Unit, Mamit District, at GSA Playground, Mamit, using the theme “Happy Childhood” for the opening of Children’s Week. Shashank Jaiswal, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Mamit, inaugurated the programme and expressed gratitude to the District Child Protection Unit, Mamit, saying that the arrangements made for Mamit’s children to spend time happily were good and wise. He said that the safety and happiness of children in our state are in everyone’s hands, and at the same time stressed the importance of cooperation between adults and the public and the need for us to work together. He said that if children in Mamit District face any difficulty, Mamit Police will always be there to help them at any time. He urged the gathering to help children create pleasant and memorable experiences, and to use such occasions to further promote child protection. The programme was chaired by Pi Vanlalruati, PO(IC), DCPU, and Dr. R. Lalrinhlua, DCPO, also spoke, saying that the Fun Day was organized for the children of Mamit town and that it is important to provide children with more free and enjoyable time. He said that since children are the future leaders of our country, it is our responsibility to care for them properly. During the Fun Day, DCPU spent time with the children using various fun activities such as Bouncy, Trampoline, See Saw, Mega Block, Ball Pool, and games like Spin the Wheel, Ball Kick, Dart Game, Cup Game, Ball Score, Photo Booth, Talent Hunt, and Bow and Arrow. Child Care Institutions also opened various stalls and presented these entertainment activities so that children could enjoy them free of cost. The children greatly valued the programme, and a large number of children from Mamit town attended.

Second Corinthians 3:16 says, “Whenever their heart turns 
to the Lord, the veil is taken away.” The heart must first be
turned to the Lord. This is real repentance. When we were fallen, 
our heart was turned away from the Lord. But when we re-
pented, our heart was turned to the Lord. This matter of turn-
ing the heart to the Lord is not done once for all. The heart

source: COMMERCE & INDUSTRIES MINISTER-IN LUNGLEIAH AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING HAWNG No.4122/2021-2022 Aizawl, the 26 th February 2022 : Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana chuan vawiin khan Electric Veng, Lungleiah NABARD sum cheng nuai 1082.93 senga ruahman Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building a hawng. Hawnna inkhawm Commerce & Industries Department Commissioner & Secretary, Pi Esther Lal Ruatkimi kaihhruaiah Dr R Lalthangliana chuan Lunglei khawpui chhunga hmasawnna ruhrel liantham, khawtlang tana chhenfakawm tak leh eizawnna kawnga tangkai taka hman theih tur Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building zawhfel a ni chu lawmawm tiin a buaipuitu Commerce & Industries thawktute, building sa tu te leh Electric Veng Lunglei khawtlang te chungah lawmthu a sawi a. C&I Department hnuaiah hmalakna hrang hrang kalpui mek zel anih thu sawiin Lunglei Supermarket sakna tur cheng nuai 1400 NEC atanga sanction hmuh anih thu sawiin Bangladesh ram nena kan insumdawn tawnna atana ruahman Integrated Check Post (ICP), Kawrpuichhuah, Tlabung ti hlawhtling turin Department chuan theihtawp a chhuah mek zel thu a sawi a ni. A Department chan dangte hnuaia hmalaknte pawh sawilangin Minister chuan MZU Southern Campus atan DPR cheng vaibelchhe 400 sawrkar laipuiah thehluh tawh niin chak taka bawhzui mek a ni a, MZU Southern Campus tana hman lailawk tur Engineering College building chei that hna pawh thawh mek a ni, a ti a. Civil Hospital Lungleia Trauma Centre sak pawh zawh fel thuai beisei anih thu sawiin Multipurpose Laboratory Building, NEC sum cheng nuai 300 a ruahman mek pawh nakum kum tir lama zawhfel beisei anih thu a sawi. Lunglei Municipal Council (LMC) chungchang pawh sawiin Minister chuan Municipal body chak tak enkawlna hnuaiah Lunglei khawpui chuan kawng hrang hrangin hmasawnna a nei dawn a ni, a ti. He huna khualzahawm Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng chuan Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building hawn theiha peih fel a ni ta chu Pathian malsawmna ropui tak a ni tiin he hmasawnna ruhrel neih theihna tura sulsutute thawhrimna leh thahnemngaihna rah a ni, a ti a. He building ti hlawhtling tura bultan tu Pu Joseph Lalhimpuia chungah leh a hmun phal taka petu Electric Veng YMA te chungah lawmthu a sawi a ni. He building sak enkawltu AIE Constructions, Tuikhuahtlang, Aizawl atangin Technical Report ngaihtlak a ni a. Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure hi NABARD, RIDF XXIII hnuaia project niin total project cost hi Rs. 1082.93 lakhs ani a. Hna hi 05/10/2018 ah thawh tan a ni. A building plinth area hi 574.875 Square metres niin building hi floor nga (5) a sak a ni a. First floor hi Agriculture leh marketing lama training leh awareness centre atan ruahman niin mihring 300 vel leng tura hisap a ni. Ground floor ah hian guest room, conference/meeting room te awmin Basement I ah hian mi 78 lenna market area bakah market office ruamhan niin Basement II ah mi 85 lenna market area niin Basement III hi motor 25 lenna parking area-a ruahman a ni. reference: AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING INAUGURATED AT LUNGLEI No.523/2021-2022 Aizawl, the 28th February 2022 : Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana on Saturday (26th February, 2022) inaugurated Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building at Electric Veng, Lunglei. The Rs. 1082.93 lakhs project is implemented under the NABARD, RIDF XXIII. Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng was the guest of honour at the inauguration. At the inaugural function chaired by Commerce & Industries Department Commissioner & Secretary, Pi Esther Lal Ruatkimi, Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana commended C&I Department staff, Electric veng YMA, VCs for their contribution towards successful completion of the project. As per Technical Report presented by AIE Constructions, Tuikhuahtlang, Aizawl, the 5 floors Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building has a plinth area of 574.875 Square metres. The first floor is intended to be used as a training and awareness centre for agriculture marketing with an estimated capacity of 300 people, with guest rooms, conference/meeting rooms at the Ground floor. Basement I and Basement II contain the market areas and market offices, with a parking area at the basement.

Lalthangliana today inaugurated the Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building at Electric Veng, Lunglei, constructed at a cost of Rs. 1082.93 lakh with NABARD funds. Lalthangliana said he was glad that the Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building, an important infrastructure for the development of Lunglei town and useful for the community and livelihood activities, had been completed. He expressed gratitude to the officials of the Commerce & Industries Department who worked on the project, the builders, and the people of Electric Veng, Lunglei. He said that various initiatives were being implemented under the C&I Department, and that sanction for Rs. 1400 lakh from NEC had been received for the construction of Lunglei Supermarket. He also said that the Department was making every effort to successfully implement the Integrated Check Post (ICP) at Kawrpuichhuah, Tlabung, which has been planned to facilitate trade with Bangladesh. Mentioning other works under his Department, the Minister said that the DPR for the MZU Southern Campus, amounting to Rs. 400 crore, had already been submitted to the central government and was being pursued vigorously, and that renovation work on the Engineering College building to be used for the MZU Southern Campus was also underway. He said that the Trauma Centre at Civil Hospital, Lunglei was expected to be completed soon, and that the Multipurpose Laboratory Building, planned at a cost of Rs. 300 lakh from NEC funds, was also expected to be completed early next year. He expressed gratitude to Pu Joseph Lalhim

No.612/2020-2021 Aizawl, 15th March,2021 : Mizoram Rajya Sabha M.P K.Vanlalvena called on Shri Venkaiah Naidu, Chairman, Rajya Sabha and Vice President of India today at his official residence and calls for the central governmentâ€™s intervention for restoration of peace in the trouble torn Myanmar, and to provide relief measures for Myanmar nationals who crossed international border to take shelter in Mizoram following gross atrocities committed against protesters who stand up for democracy, human rights and justice since the military junta took control of the Myanmar government. hypothesis: RAJYA SABHA MP PU K. VANLALVENA BRINGS MYANMAR PEOPLE’S PLIGHT TO INDIA’S VICE PRESIDENT No. 7795/2020-2021 Aizawl, 15th March, 2021: Rajya Sabha MP Pu K. Vanlalvena, who is currently in Delhi for the Parliament Budget Session, met India’s Vice President and Rajya Sabha Chairman, Pu M. Venkaiah Naidu, at his residence today and discussed the severe suffering being faced by those who are working to restore democracy in Myanmar, as well as other important needs of Mizoram. Pu Vena was accompanied by MNF Adviser Pu Rosangzuala. He informed the Vice President that many people have already been killed and injured at the hands of the military due to the unrest in Myanmar, that many people are being imprisoned, that the exact number of those killed and injured in this crisis cannot yet be known, and that the number is likely to keep increasing. He also told him that some members of the Myanmar army and police do not want to use force against the people of Myanmar, and because of that they have surrendered their weapons and, along with some other civilians, have already fled to Mizoram seeking refuge. He further conveyed that it is necessary to think about how to provide assistance to those who have fled from Myanmar, and requested the India Vice President to take steps as needed to end the suffering of the people of Myanmar. They also said that India’s central government policy toward Myanmar needs to be reviewed. Pu Vena and Pu Rosangzuala also requested the Vice President to work for the inclusion of a Mizo in the UPSC, since after India’s independence no person from Mizoram has ever been appointed as a member of the Union Public Service Commission. They informed the Vice President that even after 35 years as a full-fledged state, Mizoram is still under the AGMUT cadre in the All India Civil Service, and that it is now time to create a separate Mizoram cadre. They also requested Pu M. Venkaiah Naidu to consider allowing applicants under the Staff Selection Commission to take examinations in Aizawl instead of having to go all the way to Guwahati. When the Lord Jesus became a man, He suffered temptation as a man and passed through all the experiences of man.This man conquered;this man was victo- rious.He ascended to heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.Jesus has been “crowned with glory and honor”(Heb. 2:9). hypothesis: Throughout the world there is still one whom God has chosen, and this is what he said: “The ruler of this world is coming, and he has no claim on me” (John 14:30). In other words, in Jesus there was no trace of this world’s rulers. What we should carefully note is that when Jesus came into this world, He came not as God, but as man. God needed man. If God Himself had wanted to conquer Satan, it would have been easy enough; Satan would have fallen at once without a struggle. But God did not intend to do that Himself. He wanted man to conquer Satan; He intended the creature to conquer the creature. When Jesus became man, He endured temptation as a man and experienced every kind of human suffering. This man overcame, and this man is the conqueror. He ascended and sat at the right hand of God. Jesus was “crowned with glory and honor” (Heb. 2:9), and so He was glorified.
raw_text: Throughout the world there is still one whom God has chosen, and this is what he said: “The ruler of this world is coming, and he has no claim on me” (John 14:30). In other words, in Jesus there was no trace of this world’s rulers. What we should carefully note is that when Jesus came into this world, He came not as God, but as man. God needed man. If God Himself had wanted to conquer Satan, it would have been easy enough; Satan would have fallen at once without a struggle. But God did not intend to do that Himself. He wanted man to conquer Satan; He intended the creature to conquer the creature. When Jesus became man, He endured temptation as a man and experienced every kind of human suffering. This man overcame, and this man is the conqueror. He ascended and sat at the right hand of God. Jesus was “crowned with glory and honor” (Heb. 2:9), and so He was glorified.

reference: MIZORAM CHIEF SECRETARY LEADS GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES IN TAKING INTEGRITY PLEDGE 275/2023-2024 Vigilance Awareness Week, 2023 is to be observed in the whole of India from today, i.e. 30th October till 5th November, 2023. This year the theme is - 'Say no to corruption, commit to the Nation'. Starting off the Vigilance Week in Mizoram too, Chief Secretary Dr. Renu Sharma led the officials and staff of the Mizoram Secretariat, MINECO this morning in taking the 'Integrity Pledge' in the Secretariat Courtyard. Likewise, all Heads of Offices under the State Government also led the employees in their respective offices in taking the Integrity Pledge, in which each government servant avowed to follow probity and rule of law in all walks of life, to neither take nor offer bribe, to perform all tasks in an honest and transparent manner, to act in public interest, to lead by example exhibiting integrity in personal behavior and to report any incident of corruption to the appropriate agency. hypothesis: Under the leadership of the Mizoram Chief Secretary, the Integrity Pledge was administered in conjunction with the observance of Vigilance Awareness Week 2023, which is to be held across India from 30 October to 5 November 2023. This year’s Vigilance Week theme is “Say no to corruption, commit to the Nation.” Along with other parts of the country, this morning in Mizoram, to mark the opening of “Vigilance Week 2023,” all government employees and officials at the Mizoram Secretariat, MINECO, took the “Integrity Pledge” together under the leadership of Chief Secretary Dr. Renu Sharma. Heads of Office in every government office also administered the pledge at their respective office locations together with the officers and staff working under them. Through this Integrity Pledge, government employees pledge to firmly oppose corruption, to work honestly and transparently in accordance with government rules and orders, and, recognizing that they are serving the public, to conduct themselves and perform their duties in a humble manner worthy of emulation by others. They also pledge not to remain silent if they see or learn of any corrupt act, but to report it to the government.

Khuallian Dr. R Lalthangliana chuan Mamit District chhunga cheng te'n hriselna kawnga hma an sawn theihna tura hmanraw tangkai tak taka thuam an ni chu a lawmawm thusawiin District - 11 zinga Medical Doctor ngei District Bawrhsap, hriselna kawnga a ngaihna hria in nei chu in vannei takzet a. Aspirational District atangin Mizoram District 11- te zingah pakhatna ni thei tura tan la tura chahin in tum tlat chuan theihloh a awm lo a ni tiin kum zabi 21-a hmasawnna chu hmang tangkaiin dik taka kan hmachhawn chuan District hnufual ber thin kha a ropui ber kan ni thei a ni a ti. Dr. Thangtea chuan Pathian ringtu mizo nih hi a nuama, pi leh pute atanga lungrual tak leh inpumkhatna nena thawkho thin kan nihna chuan rah tha chhuah zelin, Covid - 19 avanga nunna chan kan nei erawh pawi hle rualin hri dona kawnga kan hmalakna-a hlawhtlinna kan hmuh mekte leh India hmarchhak State pariat (8) zingah Covid - 19 vanga thi tlemna ber State kan ni chu Pathian avang leh kan thawhhona avang a ni a ti. Minister chuan hmasawnna kan hmuh mekte chu chho zawnga thlira in delhbeh tir mai lovin hmasawnna tluantling nei turin kan tih ve theih tawk theuha tan la thar turin kalkhawmte a fuih a. Kawngpui tha nei turin hmalakna kalpui mek niin khawchhak lam atanga khawthlang lam hawiin kawngsial hna thawh tan mek a nih thu a sawi bawk. Er. H. Lalzirliana, Bialtu MLA pawhin Mamit District-in hriselna kawnga hma kan sawn theihna tur leh Aspirational District kan nihna atanga khaichhuah kan nihna tura CSR hnuai atanga hmanraw tangkai tak tak lei a ni chu lawmawm a tih thusawiin Kan District Bawrhsap-in hemi kawnga hma a lakna chu fakawm a tih thu a sawi a. Mamit District-in hriselna lama hma kan sawna, nu naupai te'n enkawlna tha zawk an dawn a, damdawi an mamawh angte an hmuh theihna tur bakah damlote enkawlna tha zawk leh rang zawk pek an nih theihna tura District chhung PHC/CHC leh Health Sub- Centre-te tana hmanraw lei hi Mamit District Bawrhsap hmalakna-in REC LTD, CSR Health Project hnuai atanga lei a ni. Vawiin-a sem tak Bolero Camper(4WD BS6) 11 lei nan hian Rs. 1,04,50,000/- hman niin Motor-te hi Health Care delivery a bik takin vaccination drive, Health camp conduct leh awareness pekna tur bakah, kawng that lohna hmun, motor naran in a thlen theih lohna khuate awlsam taka thlen theihnan 4 wheeled drive lei a ni a. HEALTH MINISTER HANDS OVER MOBILE MEDICAL VAN AND OTHER EQUIPMENT TO BE USED IN MAMIT DISTRICT, No. 7589/2020-2021

Today, Dr. R. Lalthangliana, Minister, Health & Family Welfare Department, Higher & Technical Education, Commerce & Industries, handed over a Mobile Medical Van, Essential Drugs & Diagnostic Kits, Laptops and Speakers for use at Mamit District Hospital, PHC/CHC and Sub-Centres. Speaking as the chief guest, Dr. R. Lalthangliana said that it is a great blessing that the District Superintendent, who is himself a medical doctor and understands the importance of health, is working to equip the people of Mamit District with very useful tools so that they can make progress in the field of health. He said that if we make proper use of the 21st century’s progress and face challenges correctly, there is nothing impossible, and if we strive to become one of the top districts among the 11 districts of Mizoram from among the Aspirational Districts, then the former least developed district can become the most glorious. Dr. Thangtea said that being a Mizo who believes in God is a joy, and that because we have always worked together in unity and harmony handed down from our ancestors, good results have continued to emerge. Although it is deeply regrettable that we have lost lives due to Covid-19, he said that our success in the fight against the disease and the fact that Mizoram has the lowest number of Covid-19 deaths among the eight northeastern states of India are due to God and our cooperation. The Minister urged the gathering not to be satisfied with the progress we have already achieved, but to continue working to achieve comprehensive development by doing our best. He also said that work is underway to build good roads, and that road construction from the eastern side toward the western side has already begun. Er. H. Lalzirliana, the local MLA, also said that it is commendable that useful equipment has been purchased under CSR so that Mamit District can make progress in health and benefit from being an Aspirational District. He said that the District Superintendent’s efforts in this regard are praiseworthy. He also said that although the Covid-19 pandemic is causing disruption around the world, Mizoram is among the best-performing states in India because of the strong initiatives of the government, the prayers of church members, and the efforts of community leaders. He encouraged the medical community to revive their efforts and recommit themselves in serving the public. Established in 1976, the Mizoram State Branch of IMA currently has 750 members out of which 33 are newly inducted. The organization looks after the interest of doctors as well as the well being of the community at large. It aims to promote medical and its allied sciences, improve public health and maintain honour and dignity of the medical profession.
